title: Essentiality is condition-dependent
dek: A gene required on 7H10 may be dispensable in a mouse, and conversely. Clinical importance (KatG, PncA) is not the same boolean. Lists are priors for interpreting loss-of-function, not DST.
story: Essential, in the microbial-genetics sense, means: loss of function is lethal or near-lethal in a named condition. Saturated transposon screens on rich plates mark a few hundred Mtb genes as required for axenic growth. Macrophage, hypoxia, cholesterol, and mouse spleen each move the set. Publishing “the essentialome” without the medium is like publishing a MIC without the drug.

Clinical importance is a different boolean. katG is dispensable on plates — that is why S315T and LOF exist in patients. inhA is essential in vitro; promoter mutants up-regulate it rather than knocking it out. pncA is dispensable; that is why PZA resistance is a scatter of LOF. An essentiality list is a prior for “this frameshift in a viable isolate is surprising,” not a synonym for “drug target.”

Computational use: if a viable clinical genome shows a high-quality frameshift in a core-essential gene (rpoB catalytic residues, rrs, an aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase), suspect contamination, mixed mapping, a wrong annotation, or a compensatory duplication — then look at the BAM. Do not silently drop the isolate from a transmission tree as “low quality” without saying why.
deep: In vitro essential ≈ axenic growth on a stated medium. Griffin, Zhang, DeJesus and later HMM catalogues disagree at the edges; version the list.
In vivo / infection essential: genes whose insertions drop in mice or macrophages (e.g. some iron-acquisition, gluconeogenesis). These are vaccine and drug-target priors, still not DST.
Domain essential: a gene can have an essential N-terminus and a dispensable PE repeat tail. Whole-gene calls lie.
Duplicate pathways: a “non-essential” gene may be essential in a different lineage if a paralogue is absent. H37Rv is not every L1 isolate.
CRISPRi hypomorphs (next plate) are how you study the essentials you cannot knock out with Himar1.

visual.caption: The same gene can sit in different layers depending on the condition. Clinical importance (prodrug activators, sterilizing targets) is a separate column — KatG is the teaching example of dispensable-but-critical.

example.title: katG LOF in a living patient
example.setup: A clinical WGS shows a katG frameshift at AF 0.99, depth 120. The isolate grew in MGIT. A pipeline flags “essential-gene LOF, possible contamination” because an old plate-essential list included katG in error, or a student treated all annotated enzymes as essential.

steps.title: Check the biology, not the slogan
steps.body: KatG is the INH activator and is dispensable in vitro. High-level INH-R via katG LOF is expected in living bacilli. This is not rrs.

steps.title: When the flag would be right
steps.body: A frameshift in rpoB’s catalytic core, or in an aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase, in a pure viable culture is the BAM/contamination alarm. Different layer of the hierarchy.

steps.title: Write the condition
steps.body: If you cite essentiality, name the screen (medium, HMM vs Gumbel, paper year). “Essential” without a condition is not a result.

example.takeaway: Essentiality is a condition. Clinical importance is another. KatG teaches the split.

choices: Axenically essential, therefore never lost in patients
Dispensable on plates and a common INH-resistance route, while still clinically pivotal as the activator
check.answer: Dispensable on plates and a common INH-resistance route, while still clinically pivotal as the activator
check.why: Essentiality ≠ clinical importance. LOF is the resistance mechanism.

whyWrong.A WHO Group A drug: KatG is an enzyme, not bedaquiline.

check.prompt: A gene is empty of insertions in a mouse screen but densely inserted on 7H10. The honest label is:
choices: Condition-essential in the mouse screen; dispensable on that plate medium
check.answer: Condition-essential in the mouse screen; dispensable on that plate medium
check.why: Two conditions, two boolean answers. The hierarchy plate is this sentence.

whyWrong.Proof of contamination: Opposite pattern from a core-essential LOF in a viable isolate.

check.prompt: On the hierarchy, why do TnSeq lists sit in “not a DST column”?
choices: Because insertion fitness is not a WHO mutation grade for a named drug
Because lists are illegal to cite
check.answer: Because insertion fitness is not a WHO mutation grade for a named drug
check.why: Essentiality informs interpretation of LOF in a BAM; it does not fill an S/R cell.

whyWrong.Because essentials cannot be sequenced: They can; you just may not insert in them.
whyWrong.Because lists are illegal to cite: Cite them with condition and version.
